title: kate-lsp: pick the server for a highlighting mode
summary: ServersConfig::server_for_mode returns the first server, in map order, whose highlightingModeRegex matches the highlighting mode name. An empty regex never matches. A regex that does not compile is skipped. The window calls it with the syntax definition name of the document.

lane.reason: Either lane may code this packet. It is one file, one behavior, and one test, and the rule text in this packet is the oracle. The first idle lane takes it.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: Iterate self.servers; skip an empty regex; compile with regex::Regex::new and skip an Err; return the first is_match. The test server_for_mode_uses_the_regex builds a ServersConfig with c for ^(C|ANSI C89)$ and rust for ^Rust$ and asserts ANSI C89 gives c, Rust gives rust, and Python gives None. Do not nest an if inside an if. When two arms return the same value, write one condition with ||. Add each new test at the end of the one test module of the file, before its closing brace; create that module when the file is new. Do not write a second mod tests. An item with no caller outside tests gets #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]; the packet that adds the caller removes it. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: config::tests::server_for_mode_uses_the_regex
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because server_for_mode does not exist. After the change the mode name selects the server by regex and an unknown mode gives None.
